output.myth: When the dark half is longest, the lamps along the Lamp Road burn low and smoke, and the light goes yellow and weak. Ennu the Kite-Wright, who keeps the lamp-wicks of the sky, takes up his shears of bone and sail-cord and climbs the road. Hesk at the pole counts the wicks as he goes. Each one he cuts back, so the flame comes up clean and white. Then he hangs the shears in Vel for a single night, so the people know the work is done. My grandmother saw them once, when she was a girl, just above the north shore. She said the blades were open like a bird's wings, and that you could hear them in the wind if you were quiet. The next night they were gone. Tavo the Gale had come down the road laughing and carried them off to the Unflown, where he hides what he steals.
output.verse:
Two rings and a pin,
trim the wicks, the lamps burn clean,
hung one night, then gone.
